html:
The Aral Sea, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, was once the fourth largest lake in the world. From the 1960s it shrank fast, and by the 2000s most of it had dried into desert.

The cause was irrigation. The two rivers that fed the sea, the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, were drained by Soviet canals such as the Karakum Canal to grow cotton in the desert. With little water reaching it, the sea dropped year by year and grew saltier.

  • The fishing industry died. Ports such as Moynaq were left stranded far from the water, their boats rusting on the sand.
  • Winds blew salt and farm chemicals from the dry seabed over the region, and people's health suffered.
  • Summers became hotter and winters colder around the old shore.

In 1987 the sea split into a northern and a southern part. A dam built in 2005 saved the small northern sea, but the large southern sea has mostly gone. It is one of the worst environmental disasters caused by people.
sum: The Aral Sea, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, was once the fourth largest lake in the world. From the 1960s it shrank fast, and by the 2000s most of it had dried into desert.
